candidate.answerReason: The submerged brick occupies 8000 cubic centimeters. Spreading that displaced volume over the aquarium's 4000-square-centimeter base raises the water 2 cm, agreeing with D.

methods.label: Displaced volume
methods.explanation:
The brick's height is only \(10\) cm, so it is completely underwater when placed on its base at the bottom. Its volume is
\[
40\cdot20\cdot10=8000\text{ cm}^3.
\]
The brick pushes this much water above the original water level. Because that extra layer covers the aquarium's entire base, whose area is \(100\cdot40=4000\text{ cm}^2\), the rise is
\[
\frac{8000}{4000}=2\text{ cm}.
\]
The final water height is \(42\) cm, below the \(50\)-cm rim, so no water overflows. The answer is \(2\) cm, choice D.
methods.levelReason: This uses elementary rectangular-prism volume, rectangle area, and division.

candidate.annotationRationale: Rectangular-prism volume is the cataloged target used to connect the brick's dimensions to the rising layer. Rectangle area and cubic units support the calculation. The displacement relationship itself is missing from the catalog.

needsNewNodes.name: Liquid displacement and conserved volume
needsNewNodes.description: A fully submerged solid occupies space previously available to liquid. In an upright container with constant horizontal cross-sectional area A greater than zero, inserting a solid of volume V raises the liquid by V/A when no liquid is absorbed or spilled. Check complete submersion and possible overflow.
needsNewNodes.reason: The catalog covers prism volumes and capacity but does not describe why submerged solid volume equals the volume of the layer above the original liquid level.
